short: Whig Prime Minister who oversaw the abolition of slavery and the Great Reform Act of 1832.
full:
Charles Grey, 2nd Earl Grey, was a leading Whig aristocrat who spent decades in political opposition advocating for parliamentary reform and Catholic emancipation. He finally became Prime Minister in 1830 amidst widespread social unrest and demands for broader political representation, forming a government committed to overhauling the deeply corrupt electoral system.

His defining achievement was securing the passage of the Representation of the People Act 1832 — the Great Reform Act — after a fierce constitutional battle with the House of Lords and King William IV. His administration also passed the monumental Slavery Abolition Act in 1833, definitively ending slavery throughout the British Empire before his resignation the following year.
